upstream.name: The Life Engine
upstream.author: Max Robinson
upstream.note: This engine is a fork of The Life Engine. The cell-based body plan, the grid, and the idea that evolution needs no fitness function are all his.

similar.name: The Life Engine
similar.why: Max Robinson's cell-based natural selection sim. This engine is a fork of it.

similar.name: LifeEngineExtended
similar.why: C++/Qt6 rewrite with CUDA acceleration, a WASM build and an organism construction language.

similar.name: LFE-NNUE
similar.why: Evolvable sparse neural brains, 2.5D elevation habitats and a soil nutrient cycle.

similar.name: EvolutionSimulatorV2
similar.why: Adds meat dropped on death, so carnivory has its own resource.

similar.name: Life3D
similar.why: The same grid mechanics and body plans, extended into three dimensions.

similar.name: Avida
similar.why: Self-replicating programs competing for CPU cycles. The platform most ALife papers cite.

similar.name: Tierra
similar.why: Tom Ray's 1991 simulator, where digital parasites evolved without anyone designing them.

similar.name: Polyworld
similar.why: Larry Yaeger's ecology of neural-brained agents with vision, genetics and metabolism.

similar.name: Framsticks
similar.why: Continuous 3D creatures: evolved morphology, real physics, neural control.

similar.name: Evolve 4.0
similar.why: Multicellular organisms running Forth-like genetic code under strict energy conservation.

similar.name: Darwinbots
similar.why: Bots with DNA bytecode, physical bodies, feeding ties and venom.

similar.name: BioSim4
similar.why: Evolvable neural nets under survival pressure, with the clearest write-up in the field.

similar.name: Scriptbots
similar.why: Karpathy's predator-prey world: neural brains, sensory cones, open-ended reproduction.

similar.name: Evolution
similar.why: Build a creature from bones and muscles, then watch it evolve a way to walk.

similar.name: GenePool
similar.why: Ventrella's swimbots evolve a swimming gait and a taste in mates.

similar.name: Evolved Virtual Creatures
similar.why: An open recreation of Karl Sims' 1994 paper, the ancestor of every creature sim.

similar.name: Lenia
similar.why: A continuous cellular automaton whose creatures swim, turn and hold themselves together.

similar.name: Particle Life
similar.why: Cell-like structures and locomotion out of nothing but an attraction matrix.

similar.name: Growing Neural Cellular Automata
similar.why: Differentiable cellular automata that grow a pattern and regenerate when cut.

similar.name: SmoothLife
similar.why: Conway's Life generalised to continuous space, time and state.

similar.name: POET
similar.why: Co-evolves agents and the obstacles they face, so the problem keeps getting harder.

similar.name: QDax
similar.why: MAP-Elites on accelerators: searching for behavioural diversity rather than one winner.
